name: sidebar-drag-shows-favourites-hint
description: The empty favourites grid's hint text stays hidden and out of the way at rest, appears centred in the grid only while a tab row is being dragged, and hides again whether the drag ends in a drop or a plain dragend. Read back with getComputedStyle rather than a class check, since the lifecycle class is JS but the visibility and centring it drives are CSS.

actions.expression: (() => { const grid = document.querySelector('.favgrid'); const hint = grid && grid.querySelector('.favhint'); if (!grid || !hint) { return 'missing dom'; } const box = getComputedStyle(grid); const rest = getComputedStyle(hint).display; return 'rest=' + rest + ' box-display=' + box.display + ' align=' + box.alignItems + ' justify=' + box.justifyContent; })()
actions.note: The empty grid's own box does the centring (flex plus align/justify center), read once before any drag touches it.

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.rows > .tabrow'); const grid = document.querySelector('.favgrid'); const hint = grid && grid.querySelector('.favhint'); if (!row || !grid || !hint) { return 'missing dom'; } const restDisplay = getComputedStyle(hint).display; const dt1 = new DataTransfer(); row.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragstart', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt1})); const duringDrop = getComputedStyle(hint).display; grid.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragover', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt1})); grid.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('drop', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt1})); const afterDrop = getComputedStyle(hint).display; const dt2 = new DataTransfer(); row.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragstart', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt2})); const duringEnd = getComputedStyle(hint).display; row.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragend', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt2})); const afterEnd = getComputedStyle(hint).display; return 'rest=' + restDisplay + ' duringDrop=' + duringDrop + ' afterDrop=' + afterDrop + ' duringEnd=' + duringEnd + ' afterEnd=' + afterEnd; })()
actions.note: Two lifecycles in one pass: the first ends in a drop onto the grid itself, the second in a dragend with no drop at all - a drag can end either way.
